text:
maya: FYI - after the compliance micro-rollout this morning in eu1 (default-deny + stricter L7), ~36 staging GPUs never finished node join. Keystore client logs show repeated 502 from keystore-proxy and KMS decrypts consistently timing out. Audit sink queue exploded. Anyone on network or infra seeing correlated spikes?
infra-bot: [ALERT] keystore-proxy: decrypt_timeouts eu1 - severity=high - 2026-03-23T11:03:12Z
tony: seeing same on grafana - conntrack util on natgw-b jumped from 22% -> 99% in ~90s, lots of TCP_RETRANS in packet capture to keystore subnets. Audit pipeline write failures meanwhile are backing up to S3 exporter, causing huge POST retry storms.
leo: logs indicate firewall now triggers deep packet inspection for traffic to 172.31.25.0/24. DPI is reassembling TLS and causing retransmits for our ephemeral provisioning handshakes. Not sure why KMS latencies jump only for onboarding flows (short-lived TLS).
sasha: compliance required the tighter L7 rules; we can't undo policy, but we can add a scoped exception. Proposal: add a temporary SG rule that allows provisioning-role subnets -> keystore-proxy:443 + IAM condition on the rule principal. Also enable audit sampling down to 10% for onboarding traffic to stop sink thrashing.
maya: good. can you draft the IAM condition? we need to avoid open allowlists (sec asked last quarter). Also consider enabling short-lived local cache for keystore responses during node bootstrap (ttl 30s) to reduce decrypt QPS spike.
tony: mitigation plan I pushed to staging and tested: 1) add SG exception for provisioning subnet 2) bump nf_conntrack_max on natgw hosts 3) set audit-sink sampling to 10% for tags onboarding:true 4) enable keystore short-cache (30s)
leo: command snippets I ran on natgw (linux host):
```sudo sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max=300000
sudo sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_buckets=30000
# tcp timeout to avoid long-lived entries from failed handshakes
sudo sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_tcp_timeout_established=300000```
sasha: IAM condition sketch (will open PR):
```aws iam create-policy --policy-name ProvisionerKeystoreScope --policy-document '{"Version":"2012-10-17","Statement":[{"Effect":"Allow","Action":"ec2:AuthorizeSecurityGroupIngress","Resource":"arn:aws:ec2:::security-group/sg-KEEPOUT","Condition":{"StringEquals":{"aws:SourceVpc":"vpc-eu1-provision","aws:SourceArn":"arn:aws:iam::redwood:role/provisioner"}}}] }'```
maya: nice. Tony, rough ballpark on cost if we move these 36 staging joins to us-west-3 warmpool for 90 minutes? include egress + image pulls.
tony: rough: image pulls ~1.2GB/node => 43GB total. egress cost ~ $0.18/GB -> ~$7.7. Warmup handshake extra NAT overhead / metadata calls maybe $0.30/node => ~$10. Net < $50. Cheaper than wasted GPU warm time and log egress spike.
leo: applied SG exception and audit sampling change. first 6 nodes joined successfully, KMS decrypt p50 ~120ms, p95 ~650ms (was 8-12s). conntrack dropped to 55%.
infra-bot: Incident INC-20260323-21 created: eu1 keystore/decrypt backpressure impacting fleet onboarding. Assigned: maya, leo, sasha.
maya: please add runbook steps to the incident and attach the PR link when ready. Keep exception window to 90m and revoke after scoped ACL + IAM condition are in place.
sasha: will raise short-lived sec-exception ticket sec-exc-4330 and attach the ACL PR. Also adding audit tag onboarding:true for easy filter.
leo: leaving a small troubleshooting note: when you see lots of TCP_RETRANS + SACK blocks to keystore IPs, check DPI on FW and audit sink write latency. Those two together are a common pattern for join storms.
maya: agreed. we'll do a postmortem with metrics: total joins delayed, keystore QPS, audit sink retries, natgw conntrack peaks, and dollar impact. cc @infra-bot include timeline. :thumbsup:
